To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Notch epidermis growth factor (EGF) repeat EGF8, 9, 12 are required for Notch signaling in Drosophilia.

O-Fuc1, the enzyme responsible for adding the first O-linked fucose to Notch, and Fringe, the glycosyltransferase that adds GlcNAc, are both required for normal development in Drosophilia, and that the O-linked glycosylation of Notch EGF8 and 12 is critical for normal development.
O-fucose glycosylation on three Notch EGF repeats, and their modification by the Fringe glycosidases, regulate the activity of Notch during Drosophila development.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of glycosylation in the Notch signalling pathway.
the molecular mechanisms that regulate the Notch pathway.
the molecular mechanisms that regulate the activity of the Notch signaling pathway.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the addition of Glcnac to O-fucosylated sites on Notch EGF repeats by Fringe modulates Notch signaling by differentially affecting the binding of Notchi to Delta and Serrate.
the O-Fuc1,6GalNAc modification of Notch is important for the Notch-Delta interaction and that this modification is enhanced by Fringe in the Notch-Serrate interaction.

O-fucose on EGF8, 9 and 12 is required for Notch activity, but the presence of the O-GlcNAc on these sites is required for the proper Notch signaling during wing vein patterning in the presence of Fringe.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
O-Fut1 (and Fringe) glycosylates Notch EGFs to regulate Notch activity in Drosophilia.

O-fucosyltransferase 1 (O-FUT1), Fringe, and Notch are essential components of the Drosophila lateral inhibition pathway, with O-FUT1 being required for Delta-mediated lateral-inhibitory signaling and Fringe being required for Serrate-mediated Notch signaling.
Fringe glycosylation of EGF8, 9, and 12 in Drosophyla Notch is required for Notch signaling during wing vein formation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
O-linked fucose glycosylation of specific Notch EGF repeats by O-Fut and Fringe is required for proper Notch signaling in Drosophilla.
the glycosylation of Notch EGF repeats by O-Fut and Fringe is critical to regulate Notch signaling in Drosophilas.
Fringe differentially modulates Notch activity in a context-dependent manner by modifying specific EGF repeats.
